d: Room in the house of Don Pasquale, with door at the bottom of the common entrance, and two side doors leading to the interior apartments.
Don Pasquale in grand gala followed by a Servant.
Malatesta leading by hand Norina veiled.

Don Pasquale and Norina sit down. The Servants set a table in the middle of the scene with the necessities to write. Above the table will be a bell. Notary greets, sits and draws to write. Doctor standing, to the right of the Notaro, as dictating him. Notary and sayings.
Room in the house of Don Pasquale as in Act I and II.Spread on tables, chairs, on the floor, women's clothing, clothes, hats, furs, scarves, laces, cartoons, etc.
Norina enters running and, without looking after Don Pasquale, goes out. She is dressed in a huge gala, fan in her hand. Norina is said.
Malalesta and Ernesto on the edge of the door.
Don Pasquale takes it down very slowly.
Wood in the garden next to Don Pasquale's house; on the left of the stairwelled viewer who puts in the garden, straight belvedere. Small gate at the bottom. Ernesto and Chorus inside.
Original text of Ernesto's serenade (scene six).
